title: Monotonicity of time and space bounds
statement: Suppose a word-size function $W$ is computable by a finite Turing machine within time bound $T(n)$ and space bound $S(n)$: on every Boolean input $x$, the machine produces the bit representation of $W(|x|)$ after some $t\le T(|x|)$ steps and uses at most $S(|x|)$ work-tape cells. If $T(n)\le T'(n)$ and $S(n)\le S'(n)$ for every $n\in\mathbb N$, then $W$ is computable within time bound $T'$ and space bound $S'$.
hypotheses_covered: A word-size function $W$ computable within time bound $T$ and space bound $S$
